issues.detail: The Hebrew has the participle מְשַׂחֶקֶת ('playing/rejoicing', feminine, referring to Wisdom) as a descriptive statement, not an imperative. The Vietnamese 'Hãy vui chơi' ('Let/May you play') turns it into a command addressed to someone, changing the subject and mood. The correct sense is 'I (Wisdom) was playing/rejoicing in his inhabited world.'
